families.source: UKHSA multi-agency secure-settings outbreak management plan
families.topic: prevention, definitions, notification, IMT coordination, population management, communication and data sharing in secure settings
families.page_title: Management of incidents and outbreaks of communicable disease in secure settings in England
evidence_points: The plan covers prisons, young offender institutions, immigration removal centres, secure children’s settings and approved premises.
Notifiable diseases and incidents with potential health impact should be reported to the local health protection team.
The plan defines outbreaks, clusters and rare single-case incidents requiring outbreak-like management.
Partner roles include UKHSA, NHS England, HMPPS, the Home Office, local authorities and education bodies.
Population movements, isolation, healthcare access and operational continuity require joint risk assessment.
Incident management teams coordinate investigation, control, communication, reporting and data sharing.

The page is an official GOV.UK source for prevention, definitions, notification, IMT coordination, population management, communication and data sharing in secure settings and was live-checked on 31 July 2026.
The source is intended to support evidence-based, proportionate action and should be used with current local and topic-specific arrangements.

A notification, case, cluster, symptom, setting issue or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation in Management of incidents and outbreaks of communicable disease in secure settings in England applies.
Final decisions require current incident facts, responsible-authority judgement, documented risk assessment and any applicable clinical, legal or operational evidence.

families.topic: agency and professional responsibilities within secure-setting incident management
evidence_points: The appendix assigns outbreak-management responsibilities across participating agencies.
UKHSA health protection staff provide specialist public-health leadership and advice.
Secure-setting leaders retain operational responsibilities for residents, staff and facilities.
NHS and healthcare providers support clinical assessment, treatment, testing and continuity of care.
Justice, immigration, education and local-authority partners contribute according to setting governance.
Roles should be agreed clearly so that decisions, resources and escalation routes are accountable.
